critical_path.title: Verify 'More information...' link exists and is clickable
critical_path.description: Tests if the 'More information...' link is present and navigates the user when clicked, ensuring basic navigation functionality.

steps.expected: User should be redirected to the linked page.

assertions: The link is visible on the page.
Clicking the link redirects the user to a new page.

critical_path.title: Verify 'More information...' link destination
critical_path.description: Verify that the 'More information...' link redirects to the correct URL.

steps.expected: User should be redirected to the correct URL.

assertions: The browser's URL after clicking the link matches the expected destination.

validation.title: Verify link 'More information...' is present
validation.description: This tests if the 'More information...' link is displayed on the page. Since there are no validations, this tests the presence of a key element.

steps.expected: The 'More information...' link (identified by <a> tag) is present on the page.

validation.title: Verify 'More information...' link is clickable
validation.description: This tests if the 'More information...' link is clickable and navigates to the correct destination (assuming it has an href attribute).

steps.expected: The link should be clickable and navigate to the linked page (verify by checking URL change or content of the new page).

assertions: Clicking the 'More information...' link navigates to the correct page.

security.title: XSS Injection via 'More information...' Link (assuming potential redirect vulnerability)
security.description: This test attempts to inject a malicious JavaScript payload via the 'More information...' link, anticipating a potential redirect vulnerability where the link's `href` value is not properly sanitized if dynamically generated or influenced by user input elsewhere.

steps.action: Attempt to modify the 'More information...' link to include a JavaScript payload (requires access to modify the link's destination, e.g., through a URL parameter, configuration, or other input vector that is not directly presented on the homepage but may influence it).  This step assumes a vulnerability exists that allows modification of the link's destination. If no such modification is possible via client-side manipulation or exposed APIs, this test needs adaptation or reconsideration.
steps.expected: If link destination is influenced by an unsanitized parameter, then injection will occur.
The injected JavaScript code (e.g., `alert('XSS')`) should execute.

assertions: The page should not execute arbitrary JavaScript code injected via the 'More information...' link. If the link redirects, it should redirect to a safe and expected URL without executing injected script.

security.title: Redirect Tampering via 'More information...' Link
security.description: This test assesses if the 'More information...' link is susceptible to redirect tampering. If the link's target URL is dynamically generated from user-controlled data or a configuration that can be influenced, an attacker might redirect users to a malicious site.

steps.action: Attempt to modify the 'More information...' link to redirect to an external, malicious website (requires access to modify the link's destination, e.g., through a URL parameter, configuration, or other input vector that is not directly presented on the homepage but may influence it). As before, this assumes the presence of an exploitable vulnerability.
steps.expected: If a tampered URL can be set, the link will point to the malicious URL.
The user should be redirected to the tampered URL.

assertions: The 'More information...' link should redirect to a valid and trusted URL, not a malicious or unexpected external website.
The redirect URL should be validated against an allowlist of trusted domains.
